newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Fran won't stop this wedding.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Fran won't stop this wedding.

text.p: Andrea Blake and Josh Waring are getting married, come hell or high water.

The high water came late on Thursday with Hurricane Fran's unexpected visit -- a tremendous wall of seawater that flowed into their new beach house apartment in Surf City on Topsail Island, a North Carolina barrier island ravaged by the storm's 120 mph (193 kph) winds.

With their wedding scheduled for next Saturday, Blake, 26, and Waring, 22, had begun moving into their new house just two days before Fran struck. Some of their furniture was still in the removal truck outside the door.
While the floodwater damaged the house, it threatened neither their lives nor their marriage plans -- though it has altered things a bit.
Because of Fran, they'll start out married life in Greensboro, North Carolina, many miles from the sea. Florida honeymoon plans are on hold, but the marriage goes on as scheduled.
"We're the hurricane couple. We're going through with it," said Blake. "We're very lucky."
When the hurricane threatened, the couple decided to ride it out, partly to rescue belongings they had just moved in.
At the height of the storm, water started pouring in the door and a window, flooding the entire bottom floor.
"We didn't know what to do because we didn't know how deep it was going to get," said Waring.
"The scariest part for me was when I looked out the window and saw my truck (carried by the tidal surge) coming toward the house," he said.
And did their harrowing passage through the storm test their relationship? "It's made it stronger," Waring said. "We'll talk about this for a long time."
